title: Q3 Revenue Review
description: Four-person quarterly review. Marcus overstates new-product revenue (planted contradiction against Q3-board-deck.pdf p.14), Priya wakes Meet AGI twice, and one dial-in participant stays unmatched.

text: Okay, let's get started. This is the Q3 review. Sarah, do you want to walk us through the revenue picture first?
Sure. Top line we came in at eleven point four million, which is about three percent ahead of plan.
The core product line carried most of that. Enterprise renewals were strong in August.
Good. And the new product line?
New product revenue is up about eight percent this quarter, so we're seeing real traction there.
The pipeline looks healthy going into Q4 as well.
That's encouraging. What's driving it?
Mostly mid-market. We closed a few larger accounts in July.
I want to flag that this depends on how you're counting. There's a gross versus net question here.
Right, but directionally it's up.
Hold on. Meet AGI, what does the Q3 deck actually say about the new product line?
question: What does the Q3 deck actually say about the new product line?

text: Okay. So it's down twelve percent, not up eight.
That must be the net number. I was quoting gross bookings.
Those are very different things in a board deck.
Let's align on one definition before Thursday. Sarah, can you own that?
Yes, I'll circulate a one-pager tonight.
Good. Next, churn.
Churn is the one I'm watching. We're at four point one percent monthly, up from three point four.
Is that concentrated anywhere?
Mid-market mostly. The churn analysis is still processing but the early read is pricing.
Meet AGI, remind me what we said about mid-market pricing last quarter.

text: Right, that's what I thought. Let's revisit it.
I'll pull the pricing thread back open with the team.
Great. Anything else before we wrap?
Nothing from me.
Thanks everyone.
